title: Surjective completed finite free presentation of an adic tower
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal, and T an inverse system of A-modules [def-weil-inverse-system], with level n meaning exponent n+1. Assume T_0 is finite [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], each T_n is annihilated by I^(n+1), and each successor map is surjective with kernel I^(n+1)T_(n+1). Let B be the I-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let N be a B-module equipped with an A-linear isomorphism e to lim T satisfying the completed scalar residue equation [lem-weil-pbc-adic-tower-completed-scalar-limit]. Then there exist d in N and a surjective B-linear map q from the I-adic completion of A^d to N.

source.place: Lemma 087W, proof: Surjective completed finite free presentation of an adic tower

proof.text: Use Module.Finite.exists_fin' to choose a surjective A-linear map f from A^d to T_0. Mathlib Concrete.surjective_π_app_zero_of_surjective_map lifts the images of its basis vectors to vectors w_i in lim T. The A-linear combination map p has zeroth coordinate f.

Prove surjectivity of every coordinate of p by induction. At step n+1, write R for the range of its coordinate map and J=I^(n+1). Naturality and the preceding surjectivity show R+J T_(n+1)=T_(n+1). Since 2(n+1) >= n+2, the annihilation hypothesis gives J^2 T_(n+1)=0. Multiplying the preceding equality by J yields J T_(n+1) contained in R, hence R=T_(n+1). This is the private proved helper coordinate_surjective.

For x in lim T, recursively choose coefficients a_n with p(a_n) equal to x at coordinate n. The difference at coordinate n+1 lies in the successor kernel I^(n+1)T_(n+1). Surjectivity at that coordinate and Submodule.map_smul'' lift this difference to c in I^(n+1)A^d. Set a_(n+1)=a_n+c. The shifted sequence s_0=0, s_(n+1)=a_n is adic Cauchy and gives y in the completion of A^d with nth positive residue represented by a_n. This is the private proved helper compatible_preimages; no theorem about exactness of categorical tower limits is needed.

Define v_i=e inverse(w_i). Compose the completed-ring linear combination map with Mathlib AdicCompletion.piEquivFin to construct q concretely as a completed-ring linear map. For x in N, apply compatible_preimages to e(x). The coordinate residues of piEquivFin(y) are the coordinates of a_n, by AdicCompletion.map_val_apply and factor_eval_eq_evalₐ. Apply hscalar to each summand of q(y), then use e inverse followed by e equals identity. Thus every limit coordinate of e(q(y)) equals that of e(x). Concrete.limit_ext and injectivity of e imply q(y)=x, proving surjectivity.

lean.statement:
theorem adicTower_completedFreeSurjection (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (T : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (hfinite : Module.Finite A (T.obj (op 0)))
    (hzero : ∀ n : ℕ, I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A (T.obj (op n))) = ⊥)
    (htrans : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Function.Surjective (T.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ∧
      LinearMap.ker (T.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom =
        I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A (T.obj (op (n + 1)))))
    (N : ModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I A))
    (e : (restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).obj N ≅ limit T)
    (hscalar : ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : AdicCompletion I A) (a : A) (x : N),
      AdicCompletion.evalₐ I (n + 1) r = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)) a →
      (e.hom ≫ limit.π T (op n)) (r • x) =
        a • (e.hom ≫ limit.π T (op n)) x) :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (q : AdicCompletion I (Fin d → A) →ₗ[AdicCompletion I A] N),
      Function.Surjective q
